list_queues.title: List the account's queues
list_queues.description: Every queue in the storage account, as an XML EnumerationResults document. Narrow with `prefix`, and pass `include` as "metadata" to get each queue's metadata inline. Page with the `NextMarker` element the response ends with -- pass it back as `marker`.

prefix.description: Only return queues whose name starts with this.

marker.description: Continuation token from a previous response's NextMarker element.

max_results.description: How many queues per page, up to 5000.

include.description: Set to metadata to include each queue's metadata in the listing.

output.description: An XML EnumerationResults document listing the queues.

create_queue.title: Create a queue
create_queue.description:
Create a queue in the account. Idempotent in a useful way: creating a queue that already exists with the same metadata returns 204 rather than failing, so this is safe to call on every start-up.
Queue names are 3 to 63 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and cannot start or end with a hyphen.

queue_name.description: The queue name -- 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

output.description: Empty. 201 means created, 204 that it already existed unchanged.

delete_queue.title: Delete a queue
delete_queue.description:
Destroy a queue and every message in it. Irreversible -- Queue Storage has no soft delete for queues, and the messages are not recoverable.
The name stays unusable for at least 30 seconds afterwards while the service finishes, so an immediate recreate returns 409.
delete_queue.notes: Deletes all messages with the queue. The name cannot be reused for about 30 seconds.

queue_name.description: The queue to destroy, with everything in it.

get_queue_acl.title: Get a queue's stored access policies
get_queue_acl.description:
The stored access policies on a queue, as XML. Each policy names a permission set and an expiry, and a shared access signature bound to one can be revoked by deleting the policy -- which is the only way to revoke a SAS early short of rotating the account key.
An empty document means no policies, and therefore that any SAS on this queue is free-standing and irrevocable until it expires.

output.description: An XML SignedIdentifiers document, empty when no policies are set.

put_message.title: Add a message to a queue
put_message.description:
Append a message to the back of a queue. The text is wrapped in the `<QueueMessage><MessageText>` envelope the service requires.
Whether to base64-encode the text depends on what reads the queue: the official SDKs base64 by default, so a plain string written here will not decode cleanly for them. Match whatever convention the consumer uses.
`visibility_timeout` delays the message becoming visible, which is how you schedule work for later -- up to 7 days. `message_ttl` is how long it survives unread; -1 means forever. Messages are capped at 64 KB.
put_message.notes: Maximum message size is 64 KB. Consider whether the consumer expects base64-encoded text.

message_text.description: The message content. Must be XML-safe -- escape any &, < or > it contains, or base64-encode the whole thing.

visibility_timeout.description: Seconds before the message becomes visible to consumers. 0 is immediate; up to 604800 (7 days) schedules it for later.

message_ttl.description: Seconds before the message expires unread. -1 means it never expires.

output.description: An XML document with the new message's id, insertion time, expiry and pop receipt.

get_messages.title: Receive messages from a queue
get_messages.description:
Take up to 32 messages off the front of a queue and hide them from other consumers for `visibility_timeout` seconds. The XML response carries each message's `MessageId`, `PopReceipt`, `MessageText` and `DequeueCount`.
This does NOT delete anything. Call delete_message with the id and pop receipt once the work is done; if you do not, the message reappears when the timeout expires and is delivered again. Size the timeout to how long processing actually takes -- too short and the same message gets handled twice.
A high `DequeueCount` on a message means it keeps failing, which is the signal to move it aside rather than retry forever.
get_messages.notes: Read-only in the sense that it destroys nothing, but not side-effect free: the messages it returns are hidden from other consumers until the visibility timeout expires or delete_message removes them.

number_of_messages.description: How many messages to take, 1 to 32.

visibility_timeout.description: Seconds the messages stay hidden from other consumers, 1 to 604800. Make it longer than processing takes.

output.description: An XML QueueMessagesList with each message's id, pop receipt, text and dequeue count.

peek_messages.title: Look at messages without taking them
peek_messages.description:
Read up to 32 messages from the front of a queue without hiding them and without a pop receipt. Other consumers can still take them, and nothing you peek at can be deleted -- delete_message needs a receipt that only get_messages provides.
This is the tool for inspecting a queue's backlog safely: it changes nothing and cannot accidentally consume work.
peek_messages.notes: No pop receipt is returned, so a peeked message cannot be deleted.

number_of_messages.description: How many messages to peek at, 1 to 32.

output.description: An XML QueueMessagesList with each message's id, text, insertion time and dequeue count.

delete_message.title: Delete a message after processing it
delete_message.description:
Remove a message from the queue for good. Needs both its `MessageId` and the `PopReceipt` from the get_messages call that handed it to you -- the receipt is what proves you currently hold the message, and it changes every time the message is received.
Fails with 400 if the receipt is stale, which means the visibility timeout expired and someone else has it now.

queue_name.description: The queue the message came from.

pop_receipt.description: The PopReceipt from the same get_messages response. Stale receipts are rejected.

output.description: Empty on success; 400 when the pop receipt has expired.

update_message.title: Extend a message's lock or change its contents
update_message.description:
Change a received message's visibility timeout, its text, or both. Extending the timeout is how a consumer keeps a lease on work that is taking longer than expected; rewriting the text lets a multi-step consumer record progress in the message itself.
Needs the current pop receipt, and RETURNS A NEW ONE in the response headers -- which this package does not surface, so a second update or a delete after this will fail on the stale receipt. Prefer setting a long enough visibility timeout on get_messages in the first place.
update_message.notes: The new pop receipt comes back in a response header this package does not surface, so the old one becomes unusable.

queue_name.description: The queue the message is in.

visibility_timeout.description: New visibility timeout in seconds, 0 to 604800. 0 makes it visible immediately.

message_text.description: The message's new content. Must be XML-safe.

output.description: Empty. The new pop receipt is in a response header.

clear_messages.title: Delete every message in a queue
clear_messages.description:
Empty a queue completely, leaving the queue itself in place. Irreversible and indiscriminate: it removes messages currently hidden by another consumer's visibility timeout as well as visible ones, so work in flight is destroyed.
On a queue with a lot of messages this may return 500 having deleted only some of them; call it again until it succeeds.
clear_messages.notes: Also removes messages another consumer is currently processing.

output.description: Empty on success; may need repeating on a very large queue.

get_service_properties.title: Get the queue service's logging and metrics settings
get_service_properties.description: The account-wide Queue Storage configuration as XML: analytics logging, hour and minute metrics, CORS rules and the default service version. Worth reading when you need to know whether queue operations are being logged at all before trying to audit them.

get_service_stats.title: Get geo-replication status for the queue service
get_service_stats.description:
Replication status and the last sync time for the secondary region. Only answers on the secondary endpoint of a read-access geo-redundant account; elsewhere it returns an error.
`LastSyncTime` is the useful field: everything written before it is readable from the secondary, and anything after it may not have replicated yet.
get_service_stats.notes: Only valid against the secondary endpoint of an RA-GRS account. Returns XML.

output.description: An XML StorageServiceStats document with the geo-replication status and last sync time.
